def bamboo_duel(stalks):
    """Analyze a two-player cutting game played on colored bamboo stalks.

    Position
    --------
    `stalks` is a list of 1..40 nonempty strings, each of length 1..120 over
    the alphabet {'L', 'R'}. Each string is one bamboo stalk standing on the
    ground: character s[0] is the bottom segment, s[1] sits on top of it, and
    so on upward. Each segment is owned by one player: 'L' segments belong to
    player Left, 'R' segments to player Right.

    Rules
    -----
    The two players alternate turns. On their turn, a player must pick any one
    segment OF THEIR OWN LETTER anywhere in any stalk and cut it: that segment
    and every segment above it in the same stalk are removed (the stalk is
    truncated to the part strictly below the cut; it may become empty and
    disappear). A player who has no legal move on their turn loses. Both
    players play perfectly.

    Task
    ----
    Return a tuple (outcome, i) where:

    outcome is one of four strings describing the starting position:
      'L' : Left wins regardless of who moves first,
      'R' : Right wins regardless of who moves first,
      '1' : whoever moves first wins,
      '2' : whoever moves second wins.
    (Exactly one of these holds for any position.)

    i is the smallest 0-based index such that deleting stalk i entirely,
    before play begins, leaves a position (possibly with zero stalks) that is
    a win for the second player; i = -1 if no such stalk exists. Note that a
    position with zero stalks is a second-player win, since the first player
    has no move and loses immediately.

    Bounds: len(stalks) <= 40 and each stalk has length <= 120, so the game
    tree can exceed 10**80 positions; a solution must run in well under 0.1
    seconds per input in CPython.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> bamboo_duel(["L", "R"])
    ('2', -1)
    >>> bamboo_duel(["L", "R", "LR"])
    ('L', 2)
    >>> bamboo_duel(["RL"])
    ('R', 0)
    """
